Some federations are formed when independent states agree on their own to join together and pool their sovereignty into a bigger unit, like the USA, and the states stay equally strong. Others are formed when a large country divides its power between the states and the centre, like India, Spain and Belgium, and there the centre is usually more powerful.

Alluvial soil is found in the northern plains.

Alluvial soil covers the northern plains and was laid down by the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers. Old alluvium is called Bangar and has more kanker nodules, while new alluvium called Khadar is finer and more fertile. The soil has potash, phosphoric acid and lime, so it is ideal for sugarcane and wheat and these regions are heavily cultivated and densely populated.

Soil erosion is the washing away of the top soil.

Soil erosion is the removal of the soil cover and its washing away. Normally soil formation and erosion are balanced, but human activities like deforestation upset this balance. In gully erosion running water cuts deep channels that make land unfit for cultivation, in sheet erosion water flows as a sheet over a slope and washes away the top soil, and in wind erosion wind blows loose soil off flat land.

Joint forest management involves local communities in managing and restoring degraded forests, and it began formally in 1988 when Odisha passed the first resolution. Village institutions protect degraded forest land managed by the forest department, and in return the villagers get non-timber forest produce and a share of the timber.

Dams change a river's natural flow, causing poor sediment flow and too much sediment at the bottom of the reservoir, and they fragment rivers so fish cannot migrate to spawn. Dams built for flood control have sometimes caused floods because of sedimentation, and floodplains lose natural silt fertiliser. Projects also induced earthquakes and water borne diseases, and irrigation led to salinisation. They displaced many people and led to water disputes between states.
